articles.title: From Star Wars to King Arthur: 10 European startups with names drawn from fiction, folklore and religion | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Choosing a startup name is difficult. It needs to be memorable, available as a domain and sufficiently distinctive to survive an investor’s overflowing inbox – so its no surprise to see references to famous fiction such as Dune, Start Wars and even The Matrix.
The obvious and most famous example is Palantir, named after the all-seeing stones in J.R.R. Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings – an interesting choice for a company built around making sense of vast amounts of data.
We at EU-Startups, have seen an increasing startup landscape populated by gods, guardians, legendary weapons, digital worlds, and at least one desert planet crawling with enormous sandworms.
Here are 10 European startups whose names have escaped from fiction, folklore and mythology – in alphabetical order.
Ariadne Maps (Garching, Germany) – Greek Mythology
Founded in 2019 by Georgios Pipelidis and Nikos Tsiamitros, Ariadne Maps develops location analytics technology for indoor and outdoor spaces.
Based in Garching, near Munich, the startup helps retailers, transport operators and venue managers understand how visitors move through physical environments without requiring dedicated apps or tracking hardware to be installed on users’ phones.
Its name is directly inspired by Ariadne from Greek mythology. After Theseus entered the labyrinth to kill the Minotaur, Ariadne gave him a thread that allowed him to retrace his route and escape rather than wandering indefinitely through the maze. The company has described its own location intelligence as a comparable guiding thread through complex physical spaces.
It may be one of the neatest examples in this list: a mapping company named after the woman who solved antiquity’s most notorious navigation problem.
Arondite (London, UK) – King Arthur
Founded in 2023, Arondite is building software and AI systems for defence and national security organisations. The London-based startup raised more than €10.5 million in Seed funding in May 2025, following an earlier €1.9 million pre-Seed investment involving Concept Ventures and Creator Fund.
Its co-founder and CEO, Will Blyth, previously served in the British Army and worked at Palantir and Helsing, while co-founder and CTO Rob Underhill brought experience from BAE Systems and cybersecurity company Garrison.
Arondite has not publicly confirmed a medieval naming story, but its spelling is extremely close to Arondight, the sword traditionally associated with Sir Lancelot. The weapon is better known from later Arthurian tradition and modern popular culture.
A legendary sword belonging to one of the Knights of the Round Table is an almost suspiciously appropriate reference for a DefenceTech startup.
Arrakis (London, UK) – Dune
Arrakis is emerging from stealth after raising €33 million in just over three months. The company was founded by former Accel investor Rafael Quintanilla alongside a team with experience at Palantir, Revolut, Delivery Hero, Datadog and ASML.
Arrakis develops AI agents for mission-critical industrial operations, targeting sectors including energy, aerospace, logistics and manufacturing.
The name is an unmistakable nod to Arrakis, the desert planet at the heart of Frank Herbert’s Dune. Also known as Dune, the planet is the only natural source of spice, the substance upon which the fictional universe’s economy, politics and interstellar travel depend.
For a company entering the high-stakes world of industrial infrastructure, it is a suitably dramatic choice.
The spice must flow, and apparently so must the enterprise workflow.
Babbel (Berlin, Germany) – The Bible
Founded in Berlin in 2007 by Thomas Holl, Markus Witte, Lorenz Heine and Toine Diepstraten, Babbel is one of Europe’s best-known language-learning companies.
Babbel offers a subscription-based platform offering structured lessons, podcasts, vocabulary practice and interactive speaking exercises. The company says it has sold more than 25 million subscriptions and now provides around 60,000 lessons across 14 languages.
EU-Startups included Babbel in its June 2020 overview of European language-learning apps. Its name, however, reaches considerably further back than the app economy.
Babbel takes its name from the Tower of Babel, adding an extra “b” to create its distinctive spelling. In the Book of Genesis, God gives the tower’s builders different languages, leaving them unable to understand one another and causing them to abandon the project and scatter.
The added letter also evokes “babble”, neatly combining mythology, conversation and the awkward early stages of learning a language.
Bending Spoons (Milan, Italy) – The Matrix
Founded in 2013 by Luca Ferrari, Francesco Patarnello, Matteo Danieli, Luca Querella and Tomasz Greber, Bending Spoons is a Milan-based technology company that develops and acquires digital products. Its portfolio has included well-known platforms such as Evernote, Meetup, Remini, WeTransfer and Vimeo.
EU-Startups has followed the company’s rapid expansion, including its raise of more than €500 million in 2025 and its subsequent filing for a Nasdaq IPO in June 2026.
The company has confirmed that its unusual name comes from The Matrix, specifically the scene in which a child appears to bend a spoon using only his mind. The moment leads to the film’s memorable lesson that the spoon itself is not really bending; Neo must instead recognise that the rules governing his surroundings are not as fixed as they appear.
It is a suitably mind-bending reference for a company known for reshaping established digital products. The only disappointment is that its growing portfolio is managed through software and corporate strategy rather than telekinesis.
Daedalus (Karlsruhe, Germany) – Greek Mythology
Karlsruhe-based Daedalus is applying AI, robotics and software to precision manufacturing. Founded in 2019 by Jonas Schneider, a former OpenAI technical lead, the startup operates automated factories capable of producing complex components for industrial customers.
Daedalus is one of Greek mythology’s great engineers. In Greek legend, he was an exceptionally skilled inventor, architect and craftsman, best known for designing the labyrinth that imprisoned the Minotaur. He also built the wings used by himself and his son Icarus in their attempted escape from Crete.
For a startup building advanced manufacturing systems, Daedalus is close to perfect. The only slightly awkward detail is that his most famous aviation project had a famously poor safety record. Perhaps the company should keep its robots away from the sun.
Heimdall Power (Oslo, Norway) – Norse Mythology
Founded in 2016, Heimdall Power develops technology that helps electricity-grid operators monitor power lines and make better use of existing infrastructure. Its hardware sensors, nicknamed Neurons or “Magic Balls”, gather real-time information about factors such as line temperature, weather conditions and available transmission capacity.
The Oslo-based company raised €22.9 million in Series B funding in July 2024. The round was co-led by ORLEN, NRP Zero and the Steinsvik Family Office, with participation from existing investors including Investinor, Eviny, Hafslund, Lyse and Sarsia.
Heimdall is the watchman of the gods in Norse mythology, stationed at the entrance to Asgard and gifted with extraordinary sight and hearing. The company has explicitly drawn a comparison between the mythological guardian and Heimdall Power’s role in watching over electricity infrastructure.
The original Heimdall guarded the rainbow bridge Bifröst. His technological namesake watches high-voltage power lines. The scenery may be less colourful, but the monitoring brief remains broadly similar.
Mimir (Oslo, Norway) – Norse Mythology
Mimir uses AI to automate customer support and operational tasks for e-commerce companies. Founded in 2024 by Jørgen Vartdal Halse, Jens Kristoffersen and Øyvind Monsen, the startup raised €518.3k in pre-Seed funding in June 2026.
The round was led by Sondo, with participation from angel investors connected to companies including VILLOID, Kry, Enode and Whitson. Mimir’s platform is intended to help online retailers handle repetitive enquiries and workflows while drawing on information scattered across their existing systems.
While the company has not officially made the connection, Mímir is an unmistakable figure from Norse mythology. Renowned for his wisdom, memory and counsel, he guarded a well whose waters offered knowledge. Odin famously sacrificed an eye for the opportunity to drink from it.
An all-knowing adviser is a natural mascot for an AI platform expected to answer questions quickly and accurately. Thankfully, modern e-commerce teams can access Mimir’s knowledge without surrendering an eye every time a customer asks where their parcel is.
Naboo (Paris, France) – Star Wars
Founded in 2022 by Maxime Eduardo, Antoine Servant, Lucien Bredin and Jean-Louis Villeminot, Naboo provides a platform through which companies can search for, book and manage corporate events.
The Paris-based startup has raised €86.2 million across rounds of €7.5 million, €20 million and €58.7 million, with investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Notion Capital, ISAI, Ternel and Kima Ventures.
Its name comes from the planet Naboo in Star Wars, the picturesque homeworld associated with Queen Amidala, grand palaces, rolling green countryside and the occasional trade blockade.
The company has connected that natural setting with its emphasis on organising more local events and reducing unnecessary international travel. It is a surprisingly thoughtful explanation for a name that might otherwise sound like someone booked the company retreat while binge-watching the prequel trilogy.
No word yet on whether lightsaber workshops are available as a team-building activity.
Valarian (London, UK) – Game of Thrones
Valarian develops AI infrastructure designed to help organisations deploy and manage AI. The company was co-founded by Max Buchan and Josh McLaughlin, who previously spent more than a decade at Palantir – another technology company with a famously fantasy-inspired name.
Valarian has not publicly confirmed the origin of its name, but the apparent reference is difficult to miss. Its spelling closely resembles Valyrian, the language, civilisation and legendary steel associated with Valyria in George R. R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire and its television adaptation, Game of Thrones.
The theory is strengthened by McLaughlin’s Palantir background, making another fantasy-adjacent company name feel potentially deliberate.
Either way, a name evoking an advanced but mysterious lost civilisation is suitably dramatic for an AI company – although Valarian will presumably be hoping to avoid Valyria’s rather explosive ending.
From myth to reality
From Naboo’s green plains to the deserts of Arrakis, these names do more than make companies easier to remember. They provide a miniature origin story, signalling what a startup wants to represent before anyone has read its pitch deck.
Ariadne offers guidance, Heimdall keeps watch, Mimir supplies knowledge and Daedalus builds.
Some connections are confirmed, others remain educated guesses, but all demonstrate the same useful lesson: when the available domain names are disappearing, several thousand years of stories can be a very productive place to look.

articles.title: Chinese modder gets GeForce RTX 4060 working in Windows 11 on Huawei Arm workstation — uses modified driver borrowed from an Nvidia RTX Spark
articles.text:
Chinese modder gets GeForce RTX 4060 working in Windows 11 on Huawei Arm workstation — uses modified driver borrowed from an Nvidia RTX Spark
A janky first attempt at using an RTX GPU with Windows on Arm
When Microsoft and Qualcomm launched the first Copilot+ PCs sporting Snapdragon X Elite processors, the CPU performance was beyond reproach, but whether due to immature software or underwhelming integrated hardware, the GPU horsepower left a lot to be desired. The easiest way to solve that is to hook up a discrete GPU, of course, but nobody's managed that yet. Instead, an enterprising hacker in China has become the first person to publicly get an Nvidia GeForce RTX GPU running on an Arm-based platform using Windows 11, but it's not Snapdragon, and it's not an Nvidia CPU, either, WindowsLatest reports.
We knew that the Nvidia RTX Spark processors used an integrated GPU directly derived from Nvidia's Blackwell technology, and we also knew that those machines would run Arm Windows 11, so this was bound to happen sooner or later, because that necessarily means that there is an Nvidia client graphics driver for Arm-based Windows 11 out there. That's exactly what "VoidTech" on BiliBili used for his experiment, though the experiment wasn't without some pitfalls.
Specifically, VoidTech got an Nvidia GeForce RTX 4060 8GB graphics card working in a Huawei Qingyun W510 workstation. This machine does not have a Snapdragon processor, of course; Huawei makes its own CPUs, and indeed this chip is the Kunpeng 920, created by Huawei's HiSilicon division. This chip was considered a major milestone when it was introduced in 2019, as it's a 7nm server CPU with up to 80 cores, although the specific implementation in the Qingyun W510 has "only" 24 cores.
All those cores don't help it much in gaming. As PC gamers will be well aware, CPU gaming performance is basically down to single-threaded CPU performance and system memory latency. The custom TaiShan v110 cores in the Kunpeng 920 only offer up around a sixth of the single-core performance of something like a Ryzen 9 9700X, at least going by Passmark, with the usual caveats that apply to Passmark. Combined with relatively small caches and a DDR4 memory interface that's clearly tuned for throughput, not latency, and you have a recipe for middling gaming performance. That's before we even start talking about x86 emulation penalties.
| Benchmark Comparison | Qingyun W510 + GeForce RTX 4060 8GB | Ryzen 7 5800X + GeForce RTX 4060 8GB | 
| Passmark ST / MT | 733 / 9496 | 3448 / 27671 | 
| Genshin Impact 1080p High | ~25 FPS | = 60 FPS (cap) | 
| Black Myth Wukong 1080p Medium | 21 FPS | 83 FPS | 
| 3DMark Speed Way | 2252 | 2682 | 
| 3DMark Time Spy Graphics | 6369 | 10939 | 
| 3DMark Time Spy CPU | 3402 | 10775 | 
| 3DMark Night Raid GPU | 43530 | 61080 | 
| 3DMark Solar Bay | 32373 | 49435 | 
So did it work? Well, more or less. Actually, the GeForce RTX 4060 did about half of its job flawlessly, running advanced games like the Unreal Engine 5-based Black Myth Wukong and slightly less advanced games (Genshin Impact), as well as various 3DMark tests. Most software seemed to work without any issues aside from overall weak performance due to the slow Kunpeng 920 CPU; the Wukong benchmark finished at 21 FPS, while Genshin Impact struggled to break 25 FPS and stuttered frequently. However, Arknights: Endfield refused to launch, likely due to an incompatibility between its restrictive "Anti-Cheat Expert" package and the Prism translation layer required to run the x86 Windows games on Arm Windows.
The half of its job that the RTX 4060 didn't do was that VoidTech wasn't actually able to get a video signal out of the graphics card. He notes that the graphics card was recognized, and the monitor was picked up, too. He simply couldn't get the system to properly push pixels to the monitor. This likely comes down to the Nvidia Arm driver being built specifically for the RTX Spark and thus missing the necessary code to support the HDMI and DisplayPort encoders on desktop graphics cards. To get around this issue, VoidTech used the Sunshine game streaming server and the Moonlight game streaming client (on another system) to run the Huawei machine headlessly. A janky solution to be sure, but it does seem to have worked.
There's a bit more to the video, including how VoidTech had a hard time getting Windows 11 to boot on the machine at all due to broken ACPI tables, some frustration with missing Windows 11 drivers for the HiSilicon Network Subsystem (HNS), a bit where he runs a Blender Cycles render on the GeForce RTX 4060, and a couple of Nvidia RTX demos including the Star Wars "Reflections" demo that was shown with the introduction of the RTX 20 Series "Turing" GPUs. It's an interesting saga of making hardware that was never meant to work together run on an operating system that none of it supports.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
This does somewhat bode well for RTX Spark. While you probably shouldn't expect the Cortex-X925 CPU cores in the RTX Spark to outpace the latest AMD or Intel CPUs due to still being forced to pay the Prism penalty, they're going to be a damn sight faster than this seven-year-old workstation chip. Since the drivers seem to be in good shape, the consumer laptops should indeed offer capable gaming performance when they arrive later this year—at least, as long as your game doesn't have kernel-level anti-cheat

Zak is a freelance contributor to Tom's Hardware with decades of PC benchmarking experience who has also written for HotHardware and The Tech Report. A modern-day Renaissance man, he may not be an expert on anything, but he knows just a little about nearly everything.

articles.title: Apple acelera la renovación total de los Mac, comenzando con el iMac y el MacBook Pro
articles.text:
Apple está pisando el acelerador con la renovación completa de su catálogo de Mac, una actualización que se pondrá en marcha durante el otoño y que se extenderá durante todo 2027. Los primeros modelos que tendrán nuevas versiones serán el iMac y el MacBook Pro de entrada de gama, indica Mark Gurman en un nuevo reporte.
Según publica Bloomberg, el empuje de Apple por renovar los Mac va de la mano con la creciente popularidad de los ordenadores de la marca para la ejecución de agentes de inteligencia artificial. Se indica en tal sentido que el MacBook Pro más básico, con pantalla de 14 pulgadas, será el primero de esa línea en incorporar un chip M6.
Respecto del iMac, se espera que tenga su primera actualización en dos años. El todo en uno de Apple recibió su más reciente mejora en 2024, cuando se lanzó con chip M4 de ocho o 10 núcleos de CPU y GPU. La nueva versión también estaría disponible en dos variantes, aunque no se especifica si la idea de la compañía es ofrecerlo con M5 o con el mismo M6 del MacBook Pro de entrada.
La renovación total del catálogo de Mac se iniciará con nuevos iMac y MacBook Pro
Gurman sostiene que el desarrollo de ambos dispositivos ya ha concluido, pero que su lanzamiento no se producirá hasta el otoño. De modo que recién para octubre o noviembre podríamos tener novedades reales de los nuevos iMac y MacBook Pro de 14 pulgadas, considerando los antecedentes de Apple al actualizar su familia de ordenadores.
Por supuesto que los nuevos iMac y MacBook Pro de entrada sería apenas el primer paso de la renovación que Apple prepara para el catálogo de Mac. El reporte sostiene que el plato fuerte de la actualización son los MacBook Pro tope de gama, de 14 y 16 pulgadas, que debutarán un rediseño y pantallas OLED táctiles.
Gurman menciona que estos modelos usarán los chips M5 Pro y M5 Max de los modelos actuales y que ya se están probando internamente con macOS 27.1. La idea de Apple sería estrenarlos a finales de este año o a principios de 2027, pero también se indica que la compañía ya trabajaría en sus sucesores con M7 Pro y M7 Max para estrenarlos entre finales de 2027 y principios de 2028.
Otras actualizaciones en camino
Los demás equipos que se actualizarán en el futuro cercano son:
- MacBook Air: una nueva versión con variantes de 13 y 15 pulgadas llegaría en 2027, principalmente con actualizaciones de specs. Un modelo con pantalla OLED sigue en carpeta para 2028.
- MacBook Pro de entrada con M7: sería el sucesor del modelo base que se presentaría en el otoño de 2026. Llegaría en 2027 con un diseño similar al de las variantes tope de gama que se lanzarán a finales de este año, aunque no se menciona si también tendrá pantalla OLED táctil.
- MacBook Neo: el portátil más económico de Apple, que fue un bombazo en ventas, vería una nueva generación con chip A19 Pro y más RAM. No hay precisiones sobre su lanzamiento, aunque es lógico pensar que podría llegar en 2027.
- iMac con pantalla OLED, Mac Studio y Mac mini. Estas renovaciones estarían pensadas para más adelante en el tiempo y estarían un peldaño por debajo en las prioridades de Apple. Sobre el iMac con pantalla OLED ya hubo rumores a finales del año pasado, mientras que los nuevos Mac mini y Mac Studio recibirían sendas actualizaciones de chip: M5 Pro y M6 para el primero; M5 Max y M5 Ultra para el segundo.

articles.title: Snapdragon is back on the Samsung's lightest foldable, the Z Flip 8
articles.text:
At Unpacked 2026, Samsung announced the Z Flip 8, the company’s newest clamshell handset. According to rumours, this is the last smartphone in the well-regarded Z Flip series. True or not, the device is as solid as ever.
I spent a bit of time with this smartphone, and it’s pretty similar to its predecessor, but the Cover Screen is a bit larger as the company reduced the bezels. Samsung has also made it so you can do more on the Cover Screen, allowing more apps on this smaller display. The Z Flip 8 is also the lightest folding phone, weighing 180g, and feels great to hold still.
Now, the device also uses the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 Elite, which should offer a notable power bump in power. There’s also a 50MP primary shooter, a 4,300mAh battery and 12GB of RAM.
There’s also a pretty cool feature called Fan Cam, which allows someone to focus on one person in a video. For instance, you could be at a concert, and the video will focus on the main act instead of everyone in a vertical video. However, I think it’s especially enticing on the Z Flip 8 because of its camcorder mode, which lets you hold the handset as if it were a camcorder.
In Canada, the Z Flip 8 starts at $1,549.99.

articles.title: OpenAI's AI spending spree has ballooned to $750B | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI announced Wednesday that it will spend $750 billion on infrastructure through 2030, some 25% more than it estimated earlier this year, The Wall Street Journal reported. The renewed blitz comes as its Stargate data center project appears to have stalled.
The first salvo in OpenAI’s spending spree will be a $20 billion data center campus in Georgia known as Project Camellia. The development will span 1,400 acres northwest of Savannah and will draw at least 3.2 gigawatts of power from Georgia Power, the region’s utility. The generating capacity is expected to become available between 2028 and 2032.
The AI company said it would “pay the full cost of the infrastructure and electric-service costs” for the new data center. The Georgia Public Service Commission (PSC) adopted a rule last year to prevent utilities from passing on costs associated with new users drawing more than 100 megawatts.
Georgia Power also said OpenAI will reduce its power draw by up to 1 gigawatt during periods of high demand on the grid.
OpenAI is receiving a 50% property tax abatement for 15 years from Effingham County, according to the Effingham Herald.
Neither OpenAI nor Georgia Power has said how Project Camellia will be powered. TechCrunch asked both companies for specifics but did not immediately receive a reply.
Regulatory filings might provide some clues. In December, Georgia Power received approval from the PSC to produce an additional 9,885 megawatts. The utility told the PSC it expects to have all the capacity contracted by the end of 2026. The OpenAI deal accounts for about a third of that.
Based on documents Georgia Power filed with the PSC, most of the new capacity will come from natural gas. The utility said it will build or buy from third parties about 5.8 gigawatts of natural gas generating capacity, about a quarter of which will be from more polluting simple-cycle turbines. Altogether, the new fossil fuel capacity will more than double Georgia Power’s natural gas fleet. The remainder will be supplied by grid-scale batteries and solar.
While electricity from Georgia Power is expected to start flowing in 2028, OpenAI did not give a timeline for when the first GPU will be turned on. That could happen sooner than 2028 given that OpenAI recently hired Brett Mayo to lead data center construction. Mayo previously worked at xAI, where he oversaw the Colossus data center in Memphis.
Colossus was built in record time, but it has allegedly taken its toll on local air quality, according to a lawsuit filed by the NAACP and the Southern Environmental Law Center. The xAI data center has been running dozens of unpermitted natural gas turbines, claiming exemption from federal clean air regulations.

Price-hiked iPads are a little cheaper right now

At just 54 grams, the Viper V3 Pro is impressively lightweight, yet it still manages to last 95 hours of battery life on a single charge. articles.title: From a bag of naphthol to a ₹175 crore global colour business: The Vipul Organics story
articles.text:
From a bag of naphthol to a ₹175 crore global colour business: The Vipul Organics story
Vipul Organics grew from a small dye-trading operation into a Rs 175 crore colour chemistry company exporting pigments, dyes, and specialty chemicals to more than 45 countries.
Somewhere in your home right now is probably a product coloured by chemistry from a family-run company in Palghar, Maharashtra, most Indians have never heard of. Vipul Organics doesn't sell to consumers. It sells the pigments and dyes that give colour to paints, plastics, textiles, printing ink, cosmetics, and food, quietly, to manufacturers in more than 45 countries.
A business that started with one man and a bag of naphthol
The story begins in 1968, when Pravinchandra Shah started dealing in naphthol, fast colour bases, and dye intermediates, unglamorous, technical raw materials most people never think about because they never see the finished pigment itself, only the coloured product it ends up inside. In 1972 the trading operation was formally incorporated as Vipul Dye Chem, and manufacturing followed a few years later: the company built its first plant at Thane-Belapur in 1977 to make vat dyes for Bombay's textile mills.
That first manufacturing chapter did not survive the decade. Production was suspended in 1984-85 as the Bombay textile strike gutted the customer base, and the company fell back on exports to stay alive. It restarted manufacturing at Palghar in 1991, with a single unit capable of 24 tonnes a year of Blue B Base, a modest reboot for what the company would eventually become.
The real inflection point came in 1989, when Pravinchandra's son, Vipul Shah, joined the company after finishing his chemical engineering degree. Under his direction, the business expanded methodically: from dyes into fast salts, bases, and specialty chemicals, and eventually into pigments altogether, transforming a narrow dye-trading operation into a full-spectrum colour chemistry company. In 1995, it went public on the Bombay Stock Exchange. The name change to Vipul Organics Limited was recorded in mid-2016 and adopted publicly from 2017, a name that better reflected what the business had actually become.
Built quietly, sold globally
What's striking about Vipul Organics isn't a dramatic pivot or a viral moment, it's the steady, almost invisible scale it reached through decades of specialisation. The company now runs manufacturing operations at Palghar, Tarapur, and Ambernath in Maharashtra, with a new greenfield plant underway at Sayakha, Gujarat, and maintains a representative office in Delaware, USA. Exports account for roughly 70% of revenue, reaching customers across the Americas, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East and Africa.
In FY 2025-26, the company reported standalone revenues of Rs 175.4 crore, up 7.7% from Rs 162.8 crore the previous year, with profit after tax rising 55.6% to Rs 6.92 crore, its strongest year to date.
The company has also positioned itself on environmental credentials that matter increasingly to global buyers. In 2023 it received the OEKO-TEX ECO PASSPORT for its SunPrint pigment dispersion and SunActive reactive dye ranges for the textile industry, which carries ZDHC (Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals) Level 3 status, the most stringent tier, requiring on-site assessment of chemical hazard management on top of analytical testing and safety data review. The company describes itself as India's first pigment manufacturer to reach ZDHC Level 3 across its pigment and dyestuff portfolio. It also operates a zero liquid discharge plant recycling up to 98% of effluent water and holds ISO 14001 certification.
Betting on a completely new customer base
In 2025, the company made a notable strategic move: commercialising an entirely new organic intermediate for the automotive sector, a category outside its traditional pigments-and-dyes customer base and one that took roughly 18 months of customer approval to enter. Managing Director Vipul Shah described dispatching the first commercial shipment, worth close to Rs 1 crore, within two months of receiving the order, calling it proof of both the company's R&D strength and its operational agility. Follow-up orders continued without interruption, and by late 2025 total exports of this single new product line had crossed Rs 4 crore, a strong signal for a company entering an unfamiliar industry vertical.
The diversification hasn't stopped there. In 2026 the company began commercial sales under AdiMem, a new vertical making filtration membranes for water treatment using in-house technology, aimed squarely at reducing India's import dependence in a category dominated by Chinese supply. It also signed Omya as its exclusive European distributor for its SunTone and SunCoat pigment lines.
The next generation is now stepping in too. Mihir Shah, Vipul's son and the company's Executive Director, has taken on a growing role in shaping strategy, and was named runner-up for Manufacturing Today's Next Gen Leader of the Year award in September 2024, a sign that this three-generation family business is actively planning for its sixth decade of growth rather than resting on the last five.
Why this story matters
Vipul Organics will likely never trend on social media or headline a funding roundup. It doesn't need to. It represents a different, quieter model of Indian entrepreneurial success: a family business that chose depth over visibility, compounding specialised technical expertise across three generations until a Palghar manufacturing operation became a genuine supplier to nearly a quarter of the world's countries. In an ecosystem obsessed with unicorn valuations and funding headlines, Vipul Organics is a reminder that some of India's most globally significant companies were never built to be noticed, only to be relied upon.

articles.title: Bringing Design Data Management into the Developer Workflow
articles.text:
Bridging the gap between modern development environments and enterprise EDA data management.
As digital design workflows increasingly center on modern, text-based development environments, engineers expect the same efficiency from design data management as they do from coding tools. Visual Studio Code (VS Code) has become a preferred platform for developing RTL, HDL, scripts, and verification assets, offering a flexible and extensible workspace that streamlines day-to-day engineering tasks. Yet many organizations still rely on disconnected data management processes that require engineers to switch between editors, command-line tools, and separate repositories to manage versions, collaboration, and design history.
This white paper explores how Keysight SOS for Visual Studio Code bridges the gap between modern development environments and enterprise EDA data management. By embedding version control, collaboration, governance, and configuration management directly within VS Code, SOS enables engineers to manage digital design data without leaving their preferred development environment. The solution also provides a unified framework for managing digital assets alongside analog, RF, and system-level designs, creating a connected engineering ecosystem across multidisciplinary projects.
Integrating data management into the developer workflow reduces context switching, improves consistency, and strengthens design traceability throughout the product lifecycle. Teams can collaborate more effectively, maintain better visibility into project history, and ensure that engineering knowledge is captured and governed as designs evolve.
The white paper demonstrates how aligning enterprise data management with modern software development practices enables organizations to improve productivity, support scalable digital and mixed-signal development, and accelerate time to market while protecting valuable intellectual property and engineering assets.

articles.title: Samsung passe à trois smartphones pliants : tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur les Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra et Z Flip 8 pour les précommandes
articles.text:
C’est lors de sa traditionnelle conférence Galaxy Unpacked de l’été que Samsung a levé le voile sur de nombreux nouveaux produits, dont les nouvelles itérations de ses smartphones pliants pour 2026. La surprise (qui n’en était pas vraiment une avec tous les leaks), c’est le nouveau format passeport du Galaxy Z Fold 8 pour devancer Apple. Le Z Fold 8 Ultra est donc le véritable successeur du Z Fold 7 de l’année dernière, mais avec 100 euros en plus sur la facture, tout comme le Z Flip 8 qui se contente pourtant de n’être qu’une timide mise à jour du Z Flip 7 de 2025.
Ce sont trois formats, donc trois façons différentes de les utiliser. À voir celui qui vous convient le mieux, mais c’est aussi trois prix bien distincts. Les offres de précommandes permettent d’alléger un peu la facture pour les early adopters qui souhaitent recevoir leur exemplaire dès le 4 août prochain, mais pas de stockage gratuit cette fois-ci.
Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra et Z Flip 8 : les bonus de précommande
Cette année, la marque sud-coréenne offre pour l’achat de chacun des téléphones un abonnement de 6 mois à Google AI Pro ainsi qu’une « Mystery Box » avec, à l’intérieur, des produits divers pouvant atteindre une valeur totale de 568 euros. Cependant, il y a tout de même du stockage à prix réduit sur le site officiel de Samsung : 100 euros de remise sur les versions 512 Go et 200 euros de remise sur les versions 1 To.
À côté de ça, on retrouve une offre de reprise chez la majorité des e-commerçants pour celles et ceux qui souhaitent revendre un ancien smartphone afin d’acheter le nouveau : 200 euros de bonus reprise pour le Z Flip 8 et également 200 euros de bonus reprise sur les Z Fold 8 et Z Fold 8 Ultra, comme c’est le cas chez Boulanger, qui ajoute en plus 200 euros de remise supplémentaire pour ses membres Club.
Chez Fnac, l’enseigne a lancé un code promo pour ses adhérents, ce qui permet par exemple d’avoir le Galaxy Z Fold 8 à 1 399 euros au lieu de 1 999 euros (200 euros de remise pour adhérents + 400 de remise avec le code promo FOLD8400). Le bonus reprise de 200 euros est aussi disponible ici.
Amazon ne fait cependant pas comme les autres et offre 200 euros de remise sur les trois modèles : le Z Fold 8 passe 1 799 euros au lieu de 1 999 euros, le Z Fold 8 Ultra passe à 1 999 euros au lieu de 2 199 euros et le Z Flip 8 passe à 1 099 euros au lieu de 1 299 euros. Ces offres sont uniquement réservées aux membres Amazon Prime.
Les opérateurs ont aussi leur mot à dire. Par exemple, Orange propose des remises pouvant aller jusqu’à 600 euros pour les clients existants grâce au code promo PRECOZ8. Il est même possible de payer en 12 ou 24 fois sans frais.
RED by SFR s’y met aussi ! Les client peuvent toucher le Z Flip 8 à 599 euros après remise + ODR. D’autres offres sont disponibles juste ici.
Le HONOR Magic V6 repousse les limites du smartphone pliable avec un design distinctif et robuste, des performances photo de haut niveau et une batterie généreuse conçue pour durer.
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra
C’est le plus cher de la gamme, avec un prix de départ à 2 199 euros pour la version 12+256 Go du Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, contre 2 099 euros pour le Z Fold 7. Ça monte à 2 399 euros pour 512 Go et jusqu’à 2 799 euros pour passer à 16 Go de RAM et 1 To de stockage.
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8
Ce nouveau format passeport est le moins cher des Fold puisque le tarif repasse en dessous de 2 000 euros, exactement 1 999 euros pour la version 12+256 Go, puis 2 199 euros pour 512 Go et 2 399 euros pour 1 To.
Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8
Comme d’habitude, le modèle Flip est le moins cher et ce Galaxy Z Flip 8 commence à 1 299 euros pour 256 Go. Comptez enfin 1 499 euros pour la version 512 Go.
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra : le véritable successeur du Z Fold 7
Comme dit précédemment, le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra est le vrai successeur du Z Fold 7, car il reprend exactement le même format. D’ailleurs, le terme Ultra n’est pas choisi par hasard, car la marque a choisi de remettre le meilleur de son Galaxy S26 Ultra dans ce châssis qui se plie en deux.
On retrouve donc le même Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy pour des performances de haute volée, ou encore la même capacité de batterie, à savoir 5 000 mAh, soit 600 mAh de plus que son prédécesseur. Et, le petit twist, c’est que Samsung a enfin intégré du silicium-carbone dans ses accus, ce qui permet d’augmenter la capacité sans impacter la taille de la batterie.
Côté photo, le Fold 8 Ultra reprend le capteur principal de 200 mégapixels et le téléobjectif de 10 mégapixels avec zoom optique x3 (équivalent 69 mm) du Z Fold 7. La nouveauté vient de l’ultra grand-angle de 50 mégapixels, bien évidemment hérité du S26 Ultra.
Par contre, dommage qu’il ne reprenne pas la technologie anti-reflet, qui aurait pu au moins être possible sur son écran externe de 6,5 pouces en FHD+. L’écran interne, qui apparaît une fois déplié, fait 8 pouces avec une définition QXGA+. Les deux dalles sont OLED LTPO 120 Hz. D’ailleurs, Samsung semble avoir fait des efforts sur la pliure grâce à sa technologie Flex Titanium. Sinon, sachez que le Z Fold 8 Ultra est 1 mm plus fin que le Z Fold 7, toujours bon à savoir.
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 : le nouveau format passport pour devancer Apple
Eh oui, Samsung a voulu couper l’herbe sous le pied d’Apple avec son nouveau Galaxy Z Fold 8. Vous savez maintenant qu’il ne s’agit pas du successeur du Z Fold 7, mais d’un tout nouveau format dans la gamme des smartphones pliants de Samsung. Sa principale différence est sa taille plus ramassée, similaire à un passeport quand il est plié.
Ses dimensions de 123,9 x 81,9 x 9,7 mm avec un poids de seulement 201 grammes en font l’un des smartphones pliants les plus légers et les plus compacts du marché dans cette catégorie. L’écran externe fait 5,5 pouces dans un format 10:16, et affiche une définition FHD+. La dalle interne bénéficiant du Flex Titanium monte à 7,6 pouces avec du QXGA+ en prime. Encore une fois, l’un comme l’autre est Oled avec un taux de rafraîchissement variable allant de 1 à 120 Hz.
Côté photo, on retrouve deux capteurs de 50 mégapixels, aussi bien pour le grand-angle que l’ultra grand-angle. Pas de téléobjectif sur cette déclinaison, alors qu’un capteur de 200 Mpx aurait au moins permis un meilleur zoom numérique, comme c’est le cas sur le S25 Edge. Dommage sur ce point. Samsung veut cependant vous réconforter avec une nouvelle fonctionnalité vidéo : le recadrage dynamique.
Enfin, comme sur la version Ultra, on retrouve un processeur Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 for Galaxy et l’utilisation du silicium-carbone dans la batterie, mais la capacité est ici réduite à 4 800 mAh. La recharge filaire 45 W permet de récupérer 70 % en seulement 30 minutes. La charge sans fil 20 W est aussi de la partie.
Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 : un smartphone stylé, mais timide en nouveautés
La gamme Galaxy Z Flip représente l’élégance, avec un smartphone à clapet classieux dont la recette se peaufine d’année en année. Le Z Flip 8 ne déroge pas à la règle et se contente d’améliorer quelques points, comme un châssis plus léger (180 grammes contre 188 grammes pour le Z Flip 7) et plus fin (6,1 mm contre 6,5 mm pour le Z Flip 7).
Cela passe aussi par des bordures légèrement plus arrondies pour une meilleure prise en main, mais pas de quoi révolutionner la formule existante. Il reprend même la configuration photo du Z Flip 7, à savoir un capteur de 50 et 12 mégapixels, qui était déjà reprise du Z Flip 6. Le capteur selfie est de 10 mégapixels, rien ne change là non plus.
Le pire, c’est que c’est pareil pour la batterie, toujours de 4 300 mAh et sans intégration de silicium-carbone comme les deux modèles Fold de cette année 2026. On a tout de même droit à un léger boost de puissance avec la puce Exynos 2600 reprise des Galaxy S26 et S26 Plus, mais c’est tout.
Sans surprise, les écrans font la même taille que sur le Z Flip 7, à savoir 6,9 pouces pour l’écran interne — le seul à être Oled LTPO 120 Hz — et 4,1 pouces pour l’écran externe. Ce dernier promet toutefois de s’enrichir en devenant plus malin grâce à l’IA, ce qui permettra d’avoir, entre autres, des notifications filtrées ou des actions suggérées selon le contexte.
Toutes les annonces de Samsung lors de cette Galaxy Unpacked
Pendant la conférence estivale Galaxy Unpacked de Samsung, le constructeur a dévoilé ses derniers produits en date.
Pour les smartphones pliables de la marque, ce sont bien trois modèles qui sont dévoilés par le constructeur : le Galaxy Z Fold 8, le Galaxy Z Flip 8 et Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. Vous êtes perdus dans la nouvelle gamme ? Pas de soucis, nous avons défriché les produits tout juste sortis et avons distingué leurs différences. Nous avons d’ailleurs pu prendre en main le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8.
Sur cette nouvelle gamme, Samsung intègre enfin une batterie silicium-carbone, voici les explications techniques de la marque et améliore aussi l’architecture de la charge. Encore une fois, Samsung réalise des prouesses sur son écran. Enfin nous avons fait un comparatif du Z Fold 8 face à notre maquette en impression 3D du futur iPhone pliant.
Du côté des montres connectées, Samsung dévoile deux nouveaux produits : la Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 ainsi que la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2. Notre collègue journaliste Geoffroy a eu l’occasion de tester la Samsung Galaxy Watch 2 Ultra. Vous pouvez aussi lire notre prise en main de la Galaxy Watch 9.
Et pour comparer ces nouveaux modèles avec ceux déjà existants sur le marché, nous vous invitons dès maintenant à consulter notre guide des meilleurs smartphones pliables du moment.

articles.title: Meta: adolescente desiste de processo por suposto vício em redes sociais
articles.text:
A Meta obteve um alívio em uma de suas principais disputas judiciais envolvendo alegações de vício em redes sociais. Um adolescente de 15 anos da Flórida (EUA) retirou nesta quarta-feira (22) a ação que movia contra a empresa, na qual acusava a companhia de desenvolver recursos viciantes e prejudiciais em suas plataformas.
A desistência representa uma vitória temporária para a gigante da tecnologia em meio a milhares de processos movidos por adolescentes, distritos escolares e procuradores-gerais de estados estadunidenses.
A decisão ocorre poucos meses depois de a Meta e o YouTube terem sido considerados culpados, em outro caso, por negligência e danos pessoais relacionados às características consideradas viciantes de suas plataformas.
O processo abandonado pelo adolescente era o segundo de um grupo de nove ações consideradas estratégicas, selecionadas por um juiz da Corte Superior da Califórnia (EUA) entre milhares de processos semelhantes.
Esses casos foram escolhidos por serem considerados os mais representativos e fortes de uma possível ação coletiva contra a Meta, proprietária do Facebook e do Instagram, além de TikTok, Snap e YouTube.
O julgamento estava previsto para começar na próxima semana, na Corte Superior da Califórnia, no condado de Los Angeles.
Acordos com outras plataformas
- Antes do início do julgamento, TikTok, Snap e YouTube já haviam firmado acordos com o adolescente, identificado apenas pelas iniciais R.K.C.;
- Segundo Emily Jeffcott, advogada que representa o jovem, a decisão de retirar a ação contra a Meta foi motivada pela satisfação com os acordos firmados anteriormente e pela preocupação com o desgaste de enfrentar um longo julgamento;
- “O processo foi retirado porque ele ficou satisfeito com os acordos e tinha preocupações em ‘suportar um julgamento exaustivo de várias semanas'”, afirmou a advogada. Ela acrescentou: “Estamos orgulhosos do que este caso ajudou a alcançar.”
Em nota, a Meta comemorou o desfecho. “As alegações nunca se sustentaram e este resultado deixa claro que não recuaremos em defender a empresa contra processos sem fundamento”, afirmou a companhia.
Derrota recente da Meta fortaleceu tese jurídica
A retirada da ação ocorre após uma derrota significativa sofrida pela Meta em março na mesma corte da Califórnia.
Na ocasião, uma mulher da Califórnia, atualmente com 20 anos, acusou a Meta e o YouTube de negligência e de causar danos pessoais em razão dos recursos considerados viciantes de suas plataformas. O júri concluiu que as empresas foram responsáveis pelos prejuízos sofridos pela autora e determinou o pagamento de US$ 6 milhões (R$ 30,4 milhões) em indenização.
A vitória naquele processo validou uma tese jurídica considerada inovadora: a de que sites e aplicativos de redes sociais podem causar danos pessoais aos usuários. Esse entendimento abriu caminho para que grandes empresas de tecnologia possam ser responsabilizadas financeiramente em casos semelhantes.
Por outro lado, a desistência do adolescente da Flórida indica que os processos contra as gigantes das redes sociais podem não ser tão simples quanto parecia após a decisão favorável obtida em março.
Leia mais:
- Como proteger suas redes sociais de golpistas
- Como criar um perfil único com todos os links das suas redes sociais
- Meta abre vagas no Brasil para desenvolver apps de óculos inteligentes
Milhares de ações contra empresas de tecnologia
Meta, YouTube e outras empresas enfrentam milhares de processos apresentados por adolescentes, distritos escolares e procuradores-gerais estaduais. As ações alegam que as plataformas desenvolveram mecanismos viciantes — como a rolagem infinita — capazes de estimular o uso compulsivo e provocar graves impactos na saúde mental dos usuários.
Neste mês, a Meta informou em um documento apresentado à Justiça que quatro estados estadunidenses estão pleiteando US$ 1,4 trilhão (R$ 7 trilhões) em penalidades no julgamento previsto para agosto, em Oakland, na Califórnia. O valor corresponde a praticamente toda a capitalização de mercado da empresa, atualmente estimada em cerca de US$ 1,5 trilhão (R$ 7,6 trilhões).
Além desse caso, a empresa também sofreu outra derrota judicial em março, desta vez no Estado do Novo México. O procurador-geral Raúl Torrez acusou a Meta de violar leis de proteção ao consumidor e de colocar crianças em risco ao permitir que fossem abordadas por adultos.
Nesse processo, um júri determinou o pagamento de US$ 375 milhões (R$ 1,9 bilhão) em indenizações compensatórias ao Estado. A Justiça ainda decidirá o valor de eventuais danos punitivos.
Segurança infantil ganha destaque
As ações judiciais aumentaram o escrutínio sobre as políticas de proteção infantil adotadas pelas plataformas de redes sociais.
Durante os processos, vieram a público e-mails e outros documentos internos considerados desfavoráveis às empresas, indicando que executivos — entre eles o diretor-presidente da Meta, Mark Zuckerberg — teriam ignorado alertas feitos por funcionários sobre recursos potencialmente prejudiciais para crianças.
Ao mesmo tempo, cresce a pressão para que as empresas reforcem as medidas de proteção aos menores. O Congresso dos Estados Unidos debate atualmente o projeto de lei Kids Online Safety Act, que prevê mudanças obrigatórias no design das plataformas para limitar mecanismos que incentivem o uso compulsivo.
Além disso, executivos das empresas de tecnologia devem prestar depoimento ainda este ano em uma audiência dedicada à segurança de crianças e adolescentes nas redes sociais.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Spanish energy startup Catalyxx picks Portugal for €120 million bio-based chemicals plant | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Seville’s Catalyxx, a bio-based chemicals company transforming bioethanol into alternatives to fossil-derived industrial chemicals, has selected Sines, Portugal, as the location for its €120 million commercial-scale production facility.
The development is being financed through a combination of private investment and public funding. Catalyxx was recently awarded €20 million by the Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking, a public-private partnership supporting the development of Europe’s circular bio-based industries. The funding will contribute to the Sines project and its role in reducing emissions and strengthening European chemical supply chains.
Today’s announcement follows a €3 million financing for its Seville technology centre and the pre-approval of €37 million in European Investment Bank funding for an earlier proposed industrial plant in France, indicating that the Sines project follows several stages of financing and demonstration-scale development.
“Our Catalyxx Ibérica facility represents the next step in Catalyxx’s mission to replace fossil-based chemicals with renewable alternatives that are chemically identical, fully compatible with existing industrial applications and significantly lower in carbon intensity,” said Joaquín Alarcón, Chief Executive Officer of Catalyxx.
Catalyxx’s award and production facility form part of a broader, though still relatively selective, flow of European financing into bio-based chemicals, industrial biomanufacturing and renewable substitutes for petrochemical materials during 2026.
EU-Startups has seen approximately €58 million across eight adjacent transactions, including funding for Octarine Bio’s fermentation-derived pigments, Seprify’s cellulose-based industrial ingredients, D-CRBN’s circular carbon molecules and Foamlab’s bacterial-cellulose materials.
Including Catalyxx’s award brings the indicative total to around €78.3 million.
“We are thrilled to be building our first commercial-scale plant in Portugal, and we are particularly grateful to the Portuguese Trade and Investment Agency (AICEP – Global Parques ZILS), CCDR Alentejo, Câmara Municipal de Sines, Port of Sines and Algarve Authority (APS) and all the Portuguese authorities for their support and recognition of the project’s strategic importance. This project will not only accelerate the defossilization of the chemical industry, but also position Portugal as a European leader in sustainable industrial innovation,” adds Joaquín.
Founded in 2017 by Joaquín Alarcón de la Lastra Romero, a former Abengoa executive with more than two decades of international experience in bioenergy, Catalyxx also develops its R&D activities and operates its Demo Plant in La Rinconada (Seville), focused on the production of sustainable chemicals and the research of sustainable aviation fuels (SAF).
Catalyxx’s technology converts bioethanol into what the company describes as drop-in, cost-competitive and carbon-negative chemicals. “Drop-in” chemicals are designed to be chemically equivalent to their fossil-based counterparts, allowing manufacturers to introduce them into existing production systems without replacing equipment or reformulating their products.
The company’s approach is intended to give industrial customers another source of butanol, hexanol and octanol while helping them reduce the emissions associated with their raw materials. These chemicals can be used in sectors including coatings, adhesives, plastics, solvents, personal care products and other industrial manufacturing processes.
The new €120 million plant, Catalyxx Ibérica, will produce butanol, hexanol and octanol from bioethanol. These chemicals are widely used across existing industrial applications and value chains, and the company says its production process offers a lower-carbon alternative to conventional petrochemical routes without requiring customers to change their infrastructure or compromise product performance.
The Sines project marks the next stage of Catalyxx’s industrial development, building on the work carried out at its demonstration facility in Seville, Spain. At that site, the company has reportedly validated its proprietary catalytic process under continuous operating conditions, collected operational data and developed the technical expertise needed to move towards commercial-scale production.
Catalyxx says they selected Sines due to its established industrial infrastructure, deep-water port, logistics connections and access to renewable energy. Located within one of Portugal’s principal industrial and logistics hubs, the site is expected to support the company’s plans to expand the production of low-carbon chemicals and fuels internationally.
The facility is also expected to help European chemical companies diversify their supply chains while reducing their dependence on fossil-based production.
According to Catalyxx, the Sines plant could avoid approximately 105,000 tonnes of CO₂ emissions each year.
Construction is scheduled to begin by the fourth quarter of 2026. The project is currently progressing through its final development phase, with engineering activities supported by Worley, an international provider of services to the energy, chemicals and resources industries, and Quadrante, an engineering, architecture, environment and sustainability consultancy.
The Portuguese Government has granted Catalyxx Ibérica Project of National Interest status, commonly known as PIN status. This designation recognises projects considered strategically important to Portugal’s economic development and provides access to an accelerated regulatory approval process.
Catalyxx has also secured the project’s main environmental approvals, bringing the company closer to beginning construction.
By moving from demonstration-scale operations in Seville to commercial production in Sines, Catalyxx aims to prove that renewable chemical manufacturing can operate at an industrial scale. The Portuguese facility will serve as the company’s first major commercial plant and as a base for its planned international expansion.

articles.title: Samsung regala 6 meses de Google AI Pro con sus nuevos Galaxy Z Fold 8 y Z Flip 8
articles.text:
Samsung ha presentado su nueva familia de plegables Galaxy Z. Tras meses de rumores y filtraciones, el fabricante reveló los nuevos Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra y Galaxy Z Flip 8, cada uno enfocado a un público particular. Aunque sus funciones han acaparado los reflectores, los móviles incluyen un beneficio adicional que conecta el hardware con la IA de Google.
La surcoreana diseñó esta generación con miras a ampliar la adopción de los plegables entre distintos tipos de usuario. El primero de ellos es el Galaxy Z Fold 8, que apuesta por una experiencia inmersiva a la hora de jugar o ver películas. Este móvil de apenas 201 gramos cuenta con proporciones de pantalla que se adaptan a la lectura, vídeo o juegos, así como una batería de 4.800 mAh que promete mayor autonomía que su predecesor.
Su hermano mayor, el Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, apunta al usuario premium que necesita un móvil para trabajar y entretenerse. Este plegable debuta con una pantalla principal de 8 pulgadas pensada para la multitarea y creación de contenido. Con apenas 215 gramos de peso, el Z Fold 8 Ultra incorpora un sistema de cámaras de 200 megapíxeles y una batería de 5.000 mAh que admite carga rápida de 45 W.
La oferta se completa con el Galaxy Z Flip 8, un móvil de formato compacto que alcanza los 6,1 mm de grosor. De acuerdo con Samsung, este es el plegable más fino y ligero que han fabricado hasta ahora en la familia Flip. Su gran virtud es la FlexWindow rediseñada que integra funciones de IA directamente en la pantalla exterior, permitiéndonos acceder a información y automatizaciones sin necesidad de abrir el dispositivo.
Los nuevos Galaxy Z Fold 8 y Z Flip 8 te regalan una suscripción a Google AI Pro
Los tres comparten la integración de Galaxy AI y la inteligencia artificial de Gemini. Es aquí donde la cosa se pone interesante, ya que Samsung está ofreciendo hasta seis meses de acceso gratuito a Google AI Pro para quienes compren alguno de estos tres plegables. Este plan, en condiciones normales, tiene un coste de 21,99 euros al mes (o 395 pesos mexicanos).
Si eres usuario de Gemini, seguro te habrás encontrado con algunas limitantes a la hora de usar la IA. Google restringe algunas de sus herramientas a los planes de pago más caros, incluyendo la generación y edición de video con Veo 3.1. Este modelo te permite crear clips cortos a partir de un prompt, mientras que Google Flow se enfoca en la producción de varias tomas para construir cortometrajes con IA.
El plan de Google AI Pro también otorga acceso al modelo más poderoso de Gemini, el cual tiene una ventana de contexto capaz de procesar hasta 1.500 páginas de información en una sola consulta. Además, los usuarios pueden llevar a Gemini a Documentos, Hojas de cálculo, Drive y Presentaciones, en donde la IA funciona como asistente para revisar borradores, verificar ortografía y gramática, o cruzar información entre distintos archivos.
La prueba de Google AI Pro también incluye 5 TB de almacenamiento y será válida hasta el 1 de agosto de 2027. Si compras un Galaxy Z series solamente tendrás que vincular tu cuenta para poder canjear la promoción.

articles.title: Meta to use custom AMD Instinct MI400 accelerators with 144GB of HBM4 for select workloads, report claims — could dramatically reduce cost at the expense of versatility
articles.text:
Meta to use custom AMD Instinct MI400 accelerators with 144GB of HBM4 for select workloads, report claims — could dramatically reduce cost at the expense of versatility
1/3 the memory, optimized for recommendation systems.
AMD's custom Instinct MI450-based AI accelerator for Meta will use three times less memory than the fully-fledged Instinct MI455X and will be optimized primarily for recommendation systems operated by Facebook and other social platforms, according to SemiAnalysis. If the report is accurate, it is reasonable to expect Meta to keep using Nvidia hardware for training frontier AI models and running inference.
The custom Instinct MI455X for Meta will carry 144GB of HBM4 memory using six 8-Hi packages, whereas the full-blown Instinct MI455X will be equipped with 432 GB of HBM4 memory, according to SemiAnalysis. In addition, the part will reportedly offer 'significant decreases in compute.' The new design will offer a more competitive bandwidth-per-dollar ratio for recommendation systems, but will not be optimized for training of frontier AI models or running inference, the report claims.
Cutting compute performance and reducing HBM4 capacity from 432GB to 144GB should dramatically reduce the bill of materials, as HBM4 is exceptionally expensive. Furthermore, the reduction would cut the package size of the custom Instinct MI450-series accelerator for Meta, which is another way to reduce BOM costs. By using custom cut-down Instinct MI450-series accelerators instead of fully-fledged models, Meta can potentially save tens of millions of dollars.
As added bonuses, these custom Instinct MI450-series accelerators will also consume significantly less power when running recommendation workloads without significantly reducing performance. Also, such accelerators can offer better CPU/GPU balance for recommendation systems, according to SemiAnalysis. If Meta runs these accelerators primarily on recommendation workloads for their entire useful lives, the custom design could deliver substantially better total-cost-of-ownership.
However, such cutting down has many disadvantages. The biggest problem is loss of versatility. The reductions in both compute and HBM make it less attractive for LLM training and inference. The standard Instinct MI455X has 432 GB of HBM4 and 19.6 TB/s of bandwidth, which is particularly beneficial for large-scale training and inference. By contrast, the 144 GB capacity may be particularly restrictive for modern LLM training and inference.
In addition, there is also an interchangeability problem. A general-purpose Instinct MI455X can be reassigned from recommendation workloads to training, inference, or other workloads. Meta's specialized version is less attractive outside its intended workload. If Meta's compute demand shifts toward model training and LLM inference, it may find itself sitting on a huge installed base of accelerators optimized for a different workload mix.
As a result, for Meta's model training and inference workloads, the alternative to Meta's cut-down custom MI400 would likely be full-fat AMD Instinct MI455X systems or Nvidia's high-end platforms. Meanwhile, Nvidia has chances to become an obvious beneficiary because Meta already operates massive Nvidia infrastructure. The irony in that Meta customized an AMD accelerator to reduce costs and optimize recommendation systems, but that specialization could force its frontier AI division to buy more general-purpose accelerators — potentially from Nvidia — anyway.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
When AMD and Meta inked an agreement under which the former will supply the latter with 6 GW of Instinct AI accelerators over the next five years, they did disclose that at least some of them will be custom accelerators, including custom accelerators based on the Instinct MI450 design. As it seems now, these custom AI accelerators will only be used for select workloads, not a broad set of workloads.

articles.title: I’ve tested dozens of espresso machines, but Jura’s new J10 might be the best yet for small kitchens — with cold extraction, syrup-infused milk foam, and a wake-up timer in a surprisingly compact package
articles.text:
Jura's new espresso machine packs cold brewing, delicious syrup-infused milk foam, and timed morning brewing into a surprisingly slim package — and it might be the ultimate upgrade for your small kitchen
- The Jura E10 is a new premium espresso machine from the Swiss brand
- It offers hot and cold brewing, syrup-infused foam, and Light Brew mode
- It's available now for £1,425 (about $1,910 / AU$2,720)
Jura, known for its luxury espresso machines, has just launched a new coffee maker that packs a staggering array of advanced brewing features into a surprisingly compact package. The new Jura E10 offers hot and cold brewing, syrup-infusion for flavored drinks, and a new timer that means the machine can start brewing when you wake so your favorite coffee is ready and waiting the moment you wake up.
The feature set sounds very similar to that of the Jura J10 I tested last year, which is still one of the most advanced coffee makers I've ever used. It poured a perfectly-extracted espresso, and its cold-brewed espresso was mellow and flavorful.
Its milk system was excellent as well, whether using hot or cold milk, but what impressed me most was the Sweetfoam system that mixes the syrup of your choice into the milk as it's dispensed.
Flavored coffees are usually made by pumping syrup into the cup before adding coffee and milk, which means the flavor is concentrated at the bottom. With Sweetfoam, the syrup is evenly distributed throughout the whole drink, which means you get the full flavor with every sip, and only need to use a very small quantity. You can use regular or sugar-free syrup, and during my tests I found it had the added benefit of stabilizing the milk foam so it lasts and lasts.
Perfect for small kitchens
Like the J10, the new E10 offers a huge menu of hot and cold drinks, but now they're organized into a color-coded menu that makes it easier to find the one you want.
These options now include Light Brew — a new feature not available in the J10 — which uses a smaller dose of coffee and a lower brewing temperature to prepare a drink with a less intense flavor that's ready to enjoy straight away.
The coffee-timing feature means the machine will start brewing your coffee automatically exactly when you want it to — a feature you'd normally only see on drip coffee machines. However, it's worth noting that this is only available if you also pick up the Jura Wi-Fi Connect V2 module, which adds wireless connectivity to your coffee machine and costs an additional £49.95 (about $70 / AU$100).

All of these brewing functions are packed into a surprisingly slim package that will slot more easily into small kitchens:

| Width | 12.5 inches / 31.8 cm | 10.6 inches / 27 cm | 
| Height | 13.7 inches / 34.8 cm | 13.7 inches / 34.8 cm |

The Jura E10 is available now direct from Jura and a handful of third-party stores for £1,425 (about $1,910 / AU$2,720). It's currently only sold in Europe, but the rest of the E range is available in the US, so I'm expecting it to launch there in the coming months.

articles.title: Update für Fritzbox 7510 macht DSL wieder schnell
articles.text:
Probleme mit DSL? Fritzbox-Update macht betroffenen Router wieder schnell
Mit der Fritzbox 7510 hatte Hersteller AVM, der jetzt Fritz heißt, im Jahr 2021 ein DSL-Einstiegsmodell auf den Markt gebracht, das Supervectoring-Anschlüsse mit bis zu 300 Megabit pro Sekunde unterstützt. Zuletzt hatten Nutzer:innen aber über Probleme mit ihrer DSL-Verbindung geklagt.
DSL-Probleme bei der Fritzbox 7510
Demnach soll es in bestimmten technischen Konstellationen dazu gekommen sein, dass Verbindungen unabhängig vom gebuchten Tarif auf maximal zehn Megabit pro Sekunde begrenzt wurden. Die Folge können längere Ladezeiten, langsame Downloads oder Probleme beim Streaming und Online-Gaming sein, wie PC-Welt schreibt.
Mit dem Firmware-Update FritzOS 8.26 für die Fritzbox 7510 soll dieser Fehler jetzt behoben sein. In der entsprechenden Mitteilung geht das Unternehmen auf die Probleme selbst derweil nicht ein. Das Durchführen des Updates wird aber empfohlen, auch weil bei allen Fritzbox-Updates die Sicherheitsfunktionen aktualisiert werden, wie es heißt.
Update behebt Fehler bei DSL-Verbindungen
Neben der Beseitigung der Drosselung auf zehn Megabit pro Sekunde bringt FritzOS 8.26 Verbesserungen der Systemstabilität mit sich. So soll es eine Optimierung von Verbindungen in Mesh-Netzwerken sowie mehr Möglichkeiten im Smart-Home geben. Außerdem bietet die Fritzbox nach dem Update einen Schutz vor dem Ausfall der Internetverbindung. Die Funktion Fritz Failsafe wechselt in diesem Fall automatisch auf eine Ersatzverbindung wie Mobilfunk.
Allerdings sind WLAN-Verbindungen (Wifi 6) bei der Fritzbox 7510 hardwareseitig ohnehin eingeschränkt. Denn das Gerät unterstützt hier ausschließlich das 2,4-Gigahertz-Band. In dicht besiedelten Umgebungen kann das fehlende Fünf-Gigahertz-Band zu Störungen der Verbindung führen, wie Winfuture erklärt.
Aktualisierung über Benutzeroberfläche
Nutzer:innen einer Fritzbox 7510 können das Update über die Benutzeroberfläche der Fritzbox in Gang setzen. Dazu in den Browser „fritz.box“ eingeben und zu „System“ und dort zu „Update“ wechseln. Bei allen Nutzer:innen, die die automatischen Updates aktiviert haben, sollte die Aktualisierung ohne ihr Zutun erfolgen.
Aktuell ist FritzOS 8.26 ausschließlich als Wartungsupdate für die Fritzbox 7510 verfügbar. Es ist allerdings nicht ausgeschlossen, dass weitere Router folgen. Konkrete Informationen dazu gibt es aber noch nicht.

articles.title: Chick-fil-A discloses data breach after credential stuffing attacks
articles.text:
American fast food restaurant chain Chick-fil-A is notifying an undisclosed number of customers of a data breach after their accounts were hacked in a wave of recent credential stuffing attacks.
Self-described as the third-largest quick-service restaurant company in the United States, Chick-fil-A operates a network of more than 3,000 restaurants and provides catering services across the U.S., Canada, Puerto Rico, the United Kingdom, and Singapore.
The company revealed in data breach notification letters sent to affected individuals and filed with multiple Attorney General offices that it detected the attacks after identifying suspicious login activity to certain Chick-fil-A One accounts.
As Chick-fil-A discovered while investigating the incident, the attackers targeted Chick-fil-A's website and mobile app in June.
"Following a careful investigation, we determined that unauthorized parties launched an automated attack against our website and mobile application between June 17 and June 19, 2026 using account credentials (e.g., email addresses and passwords) obtained from a third-party source," it said. "Based on our investigation, we determined on July 13, 2026 that the unauthorized parties may have accessed information in your Chick-fil-A One account."
The information exposed in the breach includes a combination of customers' names, email addresses, Chick-fil-A One membership numbers and mobile pay numbers, QR codes, the amount of Chick-fil-A credit, and the last four digits of your credit/debit card number. Additionally, the attackers may have also gained access to birth dates, phone numbers, and addresses if stored in the compromised accounts.
While Chick-fil-A didn't disclose how many customers had their accounts breached in the June credential stuffing attacks, the company told the Texas Attorney General that the resulting data breach impacts 2182 Texans and the Massachusetts AG that it affects 39 residents. Chick-fil-A also sent data breach notification letters to residents of Iowa, the District of Columbia, Maryland, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Vermont, and Rhode Island.
In credential stuffing, attackers use automated tools to breach user accounts with stolen username/password pairs, a tactic especially effective when reusing credentials across multiple platforms. The end goal is to steal personal and financial information after taking over accounts, which can later be sold to other cybercriminals or used for identity theft and other malicious purposes.
In response to the incident, Chick-fil-A logged out all impacted accounts, removed payment methods, restored Chick-fil-A One account balances, and added rewards to affected accounts as a way of apologizing. Since the accounts were compromised using stolen credentials, the restaurant chain also advised impacted users to change their passwords as soon as possible.
A Chick-fil-A spokesperson was not immediately available for comment when contacted by BleepingComputer on Tuesday about how many customer accounts were breached in the attacks.
Chick-fil-A also confirmed in March 2023 that threat actors accessed the personal information and used the stored rewards balances of over 71,000 customers after hacking their accounts in a similar wave of credential stuffing attacks between December 2022 and February 2023.

articles.title: RoboCop : Prime Video fait renaître ce héros SF culte dans une nouvelle série
articles.text:
RoboCop : Prime Video fait renaître ce héros SF culte dans une nouvelle série
Après une longue période de gestation, le projet de série RoboCop de Prime Video va enfin voir le jour.
Amazon a donné son feu vert à une série RoboCop qui sera coproduite avec Blumhouse Atomic Monster. Huit épisodes vont être réalisés à destination du service de streaming Prime Video, sous la houlette de Peter Ocko (Pushing Daisies, Black Sails) au poste de showrunner.
Un projet de longue date
C'est depuis qu'Amazon a fait l'acquisition du studio MGM en 2022 que le projet de faire une série RoboCop est en développement.
Ocko sera scénariste, producteur exécutif et showrunner de la série, tandis que James Wan, Michael Clear et Rob Hackett de Blumhouse Atomic Monster seront à ses côtés en tant que producteurs exécutifs.
On retrouvera aussi Michael Miner et Ed Neumeier, créateurs et scénaristes du film RoboCop, au même poste.
À l'image du film de 1987 réalisé par Paul Verhoeven, la série racontera l'histoire d'un géant de la technologie qui convainc une ville d'intégrer un robot surpuissant à ses forces de police — un robot dans lequel a été transférée la conscience d'un policier très apprécié, mort en service.
"J'ai toujours été un immense fan de RoboCop, alors pouvoir contribuer à transposer cet univers à la télévision est un rêve," a déclaré Wan. "Ce que Paul Verhoeven a créé en 1987 avait des décennies d'avance sur son temps, et les questions soulevées — sur la technologie, l'identité et les véritables intérêts servis par les grandes entreprises — sont devenues encore plus cruciales aujourd'hui."
"Grâce à la vision singulière et à l'approche narrative audacieuse de Peter, et en collaboration avec Ed ainsi que nos partenaires d'Amazon MGM Studios, nous tenons à honorer ce qui a rendu l'œuvre originale culte et à souligner sa pertinence dans notre monde moderne dominé par la technologie, tout en créant quelque chose d'incontestablement inédit pour un public mondial," a ajouté le producteur.
Au cinéma, RoboCop a donné lieu à une suite en 1990, puis à un troisième film en 1993, avant d'être rebooté en 2014. La télévision n'est cependant pas un terrain de jeu inédit pour la franchise puisqu'il y a déjà eu deux séries animées (en 1988 et 1998) et deux séries live-action RoboCop (en 1994 et 2001).
Cette nouvelle série RoboCop n'a pas encore de fenêtre de sortie sur Prime Video mais Les Numériques vous tiendra évidemment informé sur le sujet.
